What is the temperature of the liquid nitrogen used to freeze soil?

Liquid nitrogen is at −196 °C and evaporates in an open system: fast (about 1–3 weeks) but expensive. Brine (calcium chloride) cooling is at about −25…−40 °C, circulates in a closed loop and is slower (about 4–8 weeks).
Why is flowing groundwater dangerous in ground freezing?
It carries heat: the ice cylinders cannot close, a “window” remains in the wall
Because the brine dissolves in it
Because flowing water freezes faster and bursts the pipes
It is not dangerous, it only increases the cost of freezing
Flowing water keeps bringing heat. With brine, a flow of about 1–2 m/day can already prevent closure; then nitrogen, closer pipe spacing or grouting beforehand helps.
What is the essence of the tremie method in underwater concreting?
The end of the concreting pipe stays in the fresh concrete throughout, the concrete rises from below
The concrete is poured into the excavation from the water surface

So the concrete does not fall through the water, does not segregate, and the cement is not washed out of it. Concreting is continuous, often day and night.

Which type of cofferdam is a self-supporting gravity structure in which a steel cylinder filled with sand works “like a barrel”?
The cellular cofferdam consists of circular cells of straight-web piles filled with sand: the fill creates hoop tension in the piles, carried by the interlocks. There is no bracing inside.
